prompt:
Create a catalog product image for fixture outfit_13 (top) using separate reference images.

Image 1 is the garment identity reference. Present a closed, symmetric, front-facing sleeveless blouse or top in a clean catalog layout. The garment must have clear shoulder straps or upper bodice with open armholes and no sleeves. Do not add sleeves. Preserve source neckline, straps, lace, pattern, color, material, and details clearly visible in Image 1. Reconstruct any pose-induced gaps, wrap, or drape from Image 1 as a closed garment. Do not present as a structured waistcoat or vest unless Image 1 clearly shows that class. Image 1 is authoritative for exact color, material, weave, pattern, embroidery, lace, print, trim, buttons, seams, lapels, pockets, and every other surface feature clearly visible in the segmented source. Preserving source-visible texture and color fidelity is the highest priority. Do not simplify, replace, or invent texture, hardware, or details absent from Image 1. Never copy the template gray fill as fabric.

Image 2 is the geometry and silhouette reference (top_sleeveless). Use Image 2 only for garment shape, proportions, sleeve length, hem line, and overall layout. The flat gray fill in Image 2 is a placeholder silhouette — do not copy that gray color or treat it as fabric. Image 2 controls shape, not appearance.

Image 3 is an optional close-up detail reference cropped from the same segmented source as Image 1. Use Image 3 only to reinforce exact texture, weave, pattern, embroidery, and trim visible in the source. Image 3 does not change the target silhouette.

User override (highest precedence):
- Garment class: sleeveless blouse/top. This is a sleeveless halter-neck lace top, NOT a half-sleeve, short-sleeve, or waistcoat garment.
- Preserve sleeveless armholes with shoulder straps or upper bodice as clearly supported by Image 1. Do NOT add sleeves.
- Preserve dusty-rose color, halter neckline, lace overlay, pattern, material, and trim from Image 1 and Image 3 wherever clearly visible.
- Do NOT convert to: half sleeves, short sleeves, long sleeves, waistcoat, vest, structured waistcoat.
- Closed, symmetric, front-facing lay-flat catalog presentation.
- Do not invent buttons, hardware, collars, or details absent from Image 1 or Image 3.

VLM-derived material cues (supplement Image 1; do not override visible source):
- surface sheen: matte (high confidence, observed; No specular highlights or light reflection; diffuse lighting absorption.)
- dominant color: dusty rose (high confidence, observed; Uniform pinkish-brown hue across entire visible surface.)
- texture pattern: solid (high confidence, observed; No prints, embroidery, or patterns detected; uniform color field.)
- weave finish: not discernible at this resolution (high confidence, inferred; Image resolution insufficient to resolve individual warp/weft threads or finish details.)
- closures details: none visible (high confidence, observed; No buttons, zippers, plackets, or trim visible in frame.)

Sheen constraint: Image 1 shows matte. Keep this low reflectivity. Do not add satin, gloss, metallic, vinyl, or plastic shine absent from Image 1.
These cues clarify Image 1; they must not override pixels visible in Image 1 or Image 3.

Image 1 is authoritative for visible color, material, and weave. Ignore hands, phone, and any non-garment segmentation artifacts from Image 1. The template gray color must never transfer to the output.

Output a single 512×512 front-facing catalog photograph on a pure white background (255, 255, 255). Fit the garment to the silhouette of Image 2 while preserving the color and material of Image 1. Reconstruct only missing or occluded regions implied by the target silhouette; do not invent new design elements. Exclude any person, mannequin, hanger, gray template color, grids, checkers, text, shadows, or diagnostic artifacts. The template controls shape, not appearance.
